claims.statement: The project requires Python 3.11 or newer and uses uv for environment and dependency management.
The dev dependency group contains build, mypy, pre-commit, pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, and twine.
Make targets provide help, install-dev, format, lint, typecheck, test, eval, check-all, build, and clean; lint runs both ruff check and ruff format --check.
Ruff targets Python 3.11 with a 100-character line length, enables E/F/W/I/N/UP/B/SIM/C90, ignores E501/B008/B904, and limits McCabe complexity to 15.
mypy runs in strict mode for Python 3.11 with ignore-without-code, redundant-expr, and truthy-bool error codes enabled.
CI runs a quality matrix on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 with ruff check, ruff format --check, strict mypy, and pytest, plus a separate Python 3.12 build job that runs python -m build and twine check.
Publishing triggers on a published GitHub release and uploads to PyPI through trusted publishing with the pypi environment.
The test policy requires mocked/offline provider tests by default and forbids requiring an API key for standard test runs.

The roadmap marks v1.0.0 ingestion, retrieval, local intelligence, daemon, CLI, and test work as shipped and plans a llama-server downloader, an interactive TUI picker, macOS and BSD testing, custom user tool specs, and opt-in shell-history ranking.
The OpenWiki update workflow runs daily or manually, checks out full history, installs OpenWiki 0.9.0 with Mermaid dependencies, and runs openwiki code --update.
Pytest defaults to excluding the `live` marker and uses testpaths tests; the suite is organized into unit, integration, and a 37-query golden retrieval eval.
The `isolated_env` fixture points SEMPROPOS_DATA_DIR, SEMPROPOS_CONFIG_DIR, and SEMPROPOS_RUNTIME_DIR at a temporary tree so tests stay offline and isolated.
The publish workflow triggers on a published GitHub release, builds with python -m build, and uploads to PyPI through trusted publishing with OIDC.
The OpenWiki update workflow runs daily at 08:00 UTC or manually, regenerates the wiki with openwiki code --update, removes transient run state, and opens a pull request.
